locator: I.18 n.4 [23649]: Componens autem est causa efficiens compositi
interpretation: The passage states that the composer is the efficient cause of the composite, which is the premise: whatever unites a and b into x efficiently causes x in some respect. The componens is identified in the same paragraph as that by which things plural in themselves are united into one ('quae autem secundum se sunt plura, in unum non convenirent nisi ab aliquo componente unirentur'), which is the uniting cause of DEF-UNITING-CAUSE (Unites c a b x). The sentence is a general premise of the reductio about God ('autem'), not part of the hypothesis 'si compositus esset Deus'. The premise asserts only EfficientlyCausesIn c x r for some respect r, weaker than 'efficient cause of the composite'; it says nothing about the respect being esse (see the separate STMT-UNITING-CAUSE-CAUSES-COMPOSITE-BEING, which this sentence supports but does not state), nor about actuality or time. The paragraph's 'nihil est causa sui ipsius' is not used here; the derivation obtains distinctness from STMT-NOTHING-IS-EFFICIENT-CAUSE-OF-ITSELF.
